chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Muhammad ibn Aslam, from Ibrahim ibn al-Fadl, from Aban ibn Taghlib, who said:

I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him): 'I happen to be in one of the roads, so I see a beautiful woman, and I am not secure if she happens to be with a husband, or from the prostitutes.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'This is not upon you; rather, upon you is that you ratify her regarding herself.'

key_terms.الْعَوَاهِرِ: Prostitutes / Single women of loose conduct
key_terms.تُصَدِّقَهَا فِي نَفْسِهَا: Ratify her regarding herself / Accept her self-presumption

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic legal ruling on assuming a woman's marital status when she is unknown?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* elucidates the Shia legal principle of *istishab al-bara'ah* (presumption of innocence/availability), where outward appearance (*zahir*) serves as valid evidence for marital status in the absence of contrary proof. Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies that a man is not required to investigate a woman's hidden status (*batin*) when encountering her in public, thereby facilitating social interactions and marriage proposals based on reasonable presumption rather than absolute certainty.
